properties.areaDesc: Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued October 29 at 3:00PM ChST until October 30 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves
of 12 to 18 feet expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large
breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet expected in the surf zone. For the
Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal flooding up to 1
foot expected. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...North and east facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning and Coastal Flood Statement, from
1 AM to 4 PM ChST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM
Friday to 4 PM ChST Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from
late tonight through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous
seas. Life-threatening swimming conditions and significant beach
erosion can be expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As TY In-fa moves west-northwest toward the
far northern CNMI, seas are expected to rapidly increase due to the
large, long-period northeast swell emanating from In-fa. This will
produce dangerous surf along north and east facing reefs after
midnight tonight. As In-fa progresses, swell will become north,
then northwest, resulting in surf building over west facing reefs
Friday night. Surf will remain hazardous through Saturday
afternoon. These surf conditions will maintain a high risk of
dangerous rip currents.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Culberson, TX; Loving, TX; Reeves, TX
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 11:21PM CDT until October 29 at 2:15AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Culberson County in southwestern Texas...
Northwestern Reeves County in southwestern Texas...
Northwestern Loving County in western Texas...

* Until 215 AM CDT /115 AM MDT/.

* At 1121 PM CDT /1021 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Orla, Red Bluff Reservoir and Red Bluff.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal New Hanover
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 28 at 10:14PM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot
of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal New Hanover County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 8 AM EDT Thursday
through Thursday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from
9 AM to noon EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 9:56PM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and upstream tidal effects on the St John
River are slowing flow. At Deland, the river is forecast to crest
near Minor Flood Stage, then begin a slow decline through Action
Stage late week into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to reach a crest of 4.0 feet. It
will then fall below flood stage late in the week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon EDT.
